analysis.title: Weekly Market Directions: Central banks: action through inaction
key_insights: The Fed, ECB and BOJ kept policy rates unchanged at their October meetings, as expected. The Fed and ECB use the pause to assess more data before acting in December.
The Fed raised rates in September and is assessing the effect. Amundi thinks the Fed is buying time and has left the door open for a December hike, though it gave no forward guidance.
Chair Warsh said financial conditions are not tight, the economy is strong and inflation is 'too high', even though the Fed believes conditions are tighter than before.

Amundi argues AI-related investment is one reason the US economy stays strong. Over the long term it should lift productivity, but near-term heavy spending creates strong demand for AI products and infrastructure and may push up inflation.

The ECB held rates and believes financial conditions have tightened. Higher energy prices, plus the risk of second-round effects from energy and wage pressures (both contained for now), will drive its December and 2027 decisions.
US equities fell in the week to 30 October on weak corporate earnings, as markets questioned companies' large AI spending. European stocks gained.
Bonds gained as safe havens and yields fell across the US, Germany, France, Italy, UK and Japan. Gold declined on the week.
Investors are now looking ahead to the outcome of the US mid-term elections.

Eurozone Q3 GDP rose 0.4% QoQ, beating expectations, but Irish data flattered the preliminary reading. Excluding Ireland, growth was 0.2%. Risks are tilted to the downside from elevated energy prices and tighter financial conditions.
German business confidence rose for a sixth month, led by manufacturing, while services sentiment weakened.

US Q3 GDP grew 3.4% QoQ against a 3.2% consensus, driven by consumer spending and AI-related investment, with capex strengthening beyond tech and a large drag from net exports. Growth is likely to slow, and elevated energy prices and low savings could weigh on consumption into 2027.

Japan's September industrial production rebounded 2.2% mom, led by vehicles and machinery, while retail sales fell 0.7%. AI-related exports and investment are supportive, but high energy costs weigh on consumers and firms.
earnings_insights: US corporate earnings were described as weak in the week to 30 October, which contributed to the US equity decline. No company names or figures are given.
